extracted.intended_audience: news consumers, journalists, and website publishers seeking to understand NewsGuard's rating methodology
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and scoring methodology used to evaluate the credibility and transparency of news and information websites, producing a 0–100 score and a Nutrition Label. Covers nine weighted, apolitical journalistic criteria, non-scored site categories, and the editorial scoring process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Does not publish false or egregiously misleading content at a significant level
rubrics_metrics.description: The site does not produce false or egregiously misleading content at a level that, in NewsGuard’s judgment, signifies a clear disregard for factual accuracy; a visitor risks being significantly misled on important topics. (22 Points)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reasons a site might pass: no evidence it publishes false/egregiously misleading content that would seriously mislead visitors; factual errors are generally minor or corrected quickly; past significant false content is not currently being published in ways that would still mislead users; when quoting other sources with false claims, the site generally does not present them as fact. Reasons a site might fail: publishes false/egregiously misleading content at a level that risks misleading visitors; retains significant past false content still featured in ways that mislead (search/results, dedicated sections); states as fact claims contradicted by abundant scientific evidence; promotes unfounded conspiracy theories; quotes false claims as fact. Note: NewsGuard reviews factual statements in both news and opinion pieces (but does not judge based on viewpoint).

rubrics_metrics.name: Gathers and presents information responsibly
rubrics_metrics.description: Content providers report and present information fairly and accurately, reference multiple sources (preferably firsthand or credible secondhand), and do not egregiously distort or misrepresent information. (18 Points)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reasons to pass: reports events factually and in context; attributes information to credible sources and credits republished content; publishes verifiable claims with evidence or firsthand reporting; notes when quoted sources make false or unsubstantiated claims and includes countervailing evidence; does not repeatedly publish false/unsubstantiated claims; discloses and oversees AI-generated content. Reasons to fail: egregious distortion (quotes out of context, misuse of studies); repeated false content; regularly quotes false/unsubstantiated claims without noting; retains numerous older false claims online uncorrected; one-sided coverage without disclosure of ownership/financing conflicts; republishes without attribution; predominately anonymous sources without describing connection; publishes undisclosed or poorly supervised AI-generated content resulting in egregious errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Has effective practices for correcting errors
rubrics_metrics.description: The site regularly identifies errors and publishes clarifications and corrections, transparently acknowledges errors, and does not regularly leave significant false content uncorrected. (12.5 Points)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pass examples: regular practice of publishing at least one correction per year with visible, clearly described corrections; newer sites with no found false claims may be too new to fail. Explanations: existence of a formal corrections policy is not required. Fail examples: no evidence of at least one correction per year; repeatedly deleting or quietly editing inaccurate content instead of issuing transparent corrections; previously active corrections but none in last 12 months; only correcting as a result of NewsGuard's review; leaving significant false claims uncorrected even if minor corrections are issued.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handles the difference between news and opinion responsibly
rubrics_metrics.description: Sites that report news or a mix of news and opinion clearly distinguish opinion from news, and when reporting news do not egregiously cherry pick facts to advance opinions. Sites advancing a particular view disclose that point of view. (12.5 Points)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pass indicators: opinion content in a clearly labeled opinion section (e.g., “opinion,” “editorial,” “commentary,” “analysis”); opinion signaled in headlines with author name and colon; sites with an overall agenda disclose their perspective prominently (about page/homepage); news content generally avoids opinionated language; sites that are explicitly opinion sites label themselves and do not purport to be straight news. Fail indicators: news content frequently contains opinionated language; advancing a viewpoint via one-sided story selection without disclosure; mixing news and opinion without clear distinction; inaccurate labeling of content. Sites that are advocacy organizations and transparent about mission might receive “N/A.”

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoids deceptive headlines
rubrics_metrics.description: The site generally does not publish headlines that include false information, significantly sensationalize, or otherwise do not reflect the content under the headline. (10 Points)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pass examples: accurate, factual headlines that properly communicate the content; slightly sensational headlines that do not misdescribe facts; isolated deceptive headlines that are not frequent enough for a typical user to encounter regularly. Fail examples: frequent headlines that misrepresent or contain significant falsehoods. Sites that do not publish headlines may receive “N/A.”

rubrics_metrics.name: Website discloses ownership and financing
rubrics_metrics.description: The site discloses in a user-friendly manner its ownership and/or financing, and any notable political affiliations or financial interests relevant to coverage held by those with significant financial interest in the site. Readers should know who is funding the content and what relevant interests owners/funders might have. (7.5 Points)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pass reasons: clearly identifies owner in a prominent, accessible section; discloses notable political/financial affiliations or conflicts of owners/funders; discloses ownership/financing in stories when relevant; nonprofit sites identify major donors accessibly. Fail reasons: does not clearly identify owner or parent company; ownership only in obscure places (copyright, ToS); nonprofit does not identify major donors; does not disclose conflicts of interest in stories related to owner/funder.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clearly labels advertising
rubrics_metrics.description: The site makes clear which content is paid for and which is not, distinguishing advertising from editorial content with clear visual cues or explicit labels. (7.5 Points)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pass examples: explicit labels like “advertisement,” “paid content,” “sponsored”; sponsored/promo articles clearly disclosed at or near the headline or start of article; disclosures for commercial partnerships or affiliate links are prominent and understandable by average readers. Fail examples: presenting sponsored/promotional articles alongside news without clear distinction; affiliate links without clear disclosure; labeling commercial content in ways an average reader would not understand (e.g., “From Our Partners”); paid promotional articles run without disclosure of the commercial relationship. Sites without ads or sponsored content may receive “N/A.”

rubrics_metrics.name: Reveals who’s in charge, including possible conflicts of interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Those in charge of editorial content are identified on the site and there is a way for readers to contact the site about editorial issues; editorial leaders’ relevant conflicts are disclosed. (5 Points)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pass reasons: identifies someone in charge of editorial decisions in an easily accessible section and provides contact method for editorial issues; discloses significant potential conflicts (e.g., political campaign involvement) of editorial leaders. Fail reasons: does not identify who oversees editorial content or only does so in hard-to-find places; lists names but provides no contact method; editorial leaders have significant undisclosed conflicts of interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provides names of content creators with contact or biographical information
rubrics_metrics.description: Content is typically attributed to an author or content creator whose full name is provided, and the site provides either contact information or relevant biographical information for most content creators. (5 Points)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pass reasons: articles are bylined with full names and provide contact info or relevant bios; if not bylined, site offers a staff directory with names, bios, contact info, and coverage areas; disclosure if content is regularly produced by AI. Fail reasons: content rarely or never attributed to specific authors; bylines use only first names, initials, or pseudonyms; authors listed but no contact or biographical information; evidence of regular AI production without disclosure or AI content attributed to human writers. Note: NewsGuard recognizes exceptions where naming journalists may be impractical due to danger, which can affect scoring (e.g., 95 Green vs 100).

rubrics_metrics.name: Score and rating levels (0–100 and descriptive bands)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sites receive a 0–100 score (weighted sum of nine criteria) and a rating level describing adherence: 100 = High Credibility; 75–99 = Generally Credible; 60–74 = Credible with Exceptions; 40–59 = Proceed with Caution; 0–39 = Proceed with Maximum Caution. Some sites may receive a non-scored designation (satire or platform).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Score is displayed in NewsGuard’s browser extension next to links. Each band has a short explanatory phrase (e.g., 'This website adheres to all nine standards' for 100). Nutrition Labels explain the site’s score and provide evidence. Scores are apolitical and points add to 100 based on criterion weights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Satire and Platform designations (non-scored categories)
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain sites are not scored using the nine criteria because the criteria do not apply: Satire (humor/satire sites that are not traditional news) and Platform (sites primarily hosting user content with limited vetting and little original content). These sites receive descriptive Nutrition Labels but no 0–100 score.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Satire: described as humor/satire; NewsGuard provides description and, if possible, who is behind it. Platform: assigned when content is user-published, presented as unvetted, and site lacks significant original content; NewsGuard describes the site and its practices. Information from such sites may or may not be reliable; they are not scored on the nine criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pass-fail scoring, weighting, and N/A rule
rubrics_metrics.description: All nine criteria are scored pass-fail: a site either receives all the points for a criterion or none. Each criterion has a different weight and the points add to 100. In some instances a criterion may be marked “N/A” if it does not apply, in which case the publisher receives the points for that criterion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NewsGuard acknowledges that pass-fail scoring can make scores less precise but argues partial points are not feasible at scale. The criteria are listed in order of importance. Sites categorized as satire or platforms are excluded from this scoring. Examples of N/A: criterion not applicable because the site does not publish headlines or advertisements, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scoring process, Nutrition Label, and editorial review
rubrics_metrics.description: Analysts (trained journalists) assess sites against the nine criteria, draft a Nutrition Label explaining judgments, contact the site for comment if it may fail criteria, and submit the label for review and fact-checking by senior editors and co-CEOs before publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nutrition Labels include a grid of the nine criteria showing pass/fail, a written explanation, evidence and examples, any publisher comments, and rating history. NewsGuard’s practice is to call the website for comment when failures are suspected and include publisher comments in the Nutrition Label. Each label is reviewed and fact-checked by experienced editors; at least one senior editor and NewsGuard’s co-CEOs review every label before publication. Scores are updated periodically if a site changes practices; changes and publisher responses may be noted via editor’s notes or published complaints. NewsGuard publishes the names of the analysts and editors who worked on the rating and provides background on staff for accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apolitical application and equal treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: The nine criteria are applied equally and are apolitical: performance on criteria should be independent of topic, tone, political leaning, or size of the news operation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: there is no partisan way to have a systemic, transparent process for corrections; indicators and rules apply to large legacy outlets and small startups alike. NewsGuard emphasizes consistent application across site types and topics.
